explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. David says the one who walks with integrity also "practices righteousness" (Psalm 15:2). Notice the word practices. It's something you keep doing, like pressing a stamp into dough batch after batch. Nobody gets good at it by doing it once and taking a nap.

It's actually true. Psalm 15:2 says he "…walks with integrity and practices righteousness…" Those two go together in the same breath. Practices means he keeps at it, like a baker who shows up to the oven every single day, even the days the dough is acting up.

explanations.answer: Honesty that goes all the way down
explanations.explanation: That's it. David says he "…speaks the truth from his heart…" (Psalm 15:2). The truth starts down deep, so it isn't just a nice coat of frosting on top. What's inside is the same as what comes out.

explanations.answer: Honesty that waits for the right crowd
explanations.explanation: Close, but the psalm doesn't say that. David says he "…speaks the truth from his heart…" (Psalm 15:2). Heart means the truth lives deep inside him, so there's no crowd to wait for. I've seen people who are honest only when somebody's watching, and the psalm is describing something much sturdier.

explanations.answer: Honesty that kicks in under pressure
explanations.explanation: Good guess, but it's not what the verse says. David says the truth comes "…from his heart…" (Psalm 15:2). That means it's already in there before any pressure shows up. It's like chocolate chips baked into the dough instead of sprinkled on at the last second.

Right on, baker. David says this person "…does no harm to his neighbor…" (Psalm 15:3). Easy to be nice to strangers you'll never see again. Being kind to the people you keep running into, week after week? That's the real test.
It's actually true. Psalm 15:3 says he "…does no harm to his neighbor…" That's a person he's around and could easily wrong. I think that's why this one lands so hard.
Careful, friend, this one flips it. Psalm 15:3 says he "…casts no scorn on his friend…" So the statement is false. He doesn't sneer at the people closest to him.

Yes, you caught it. David says he "…casts no scorn on his friend…" (Psalm 15:3). Scorn is looking down on somebody, and he doesn't do that to his friends. I'd say the friend who never rolls his eyes at you is worth more than a whole tray of warm cookies.
That's the one. David says he "…honors those who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 15:4). So he despises the vile and honors the people who fear the LORD. His respect goes to the right place.

Nope, money isn't what this verse names. David says he "…honors those who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 15:4). Great wealth isn't the group the psalm points to here. The honor goes to those who fear the LORD.
Not quite, friend. The verse says he "…honors those who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 15:4). Armies don't show up in this psalm. The group David names is those who fear the LORD.
Not in Psalm 15. David says he "…does not revise a costly oath…" (Psalm 15:4). So he keeps his word even when it costs him. Sure, he can feel the cost, but he doesn't go back and change the deal.

Right. The psalm says he "…does not revise a costly oath…" (Psalm 15:4). Costly means keeping it hurts, and he keeps it anyway. It's like a baker who promised a dozen boxes, found out it'd take all night, and kept the oven on.
That's the one. David says he "…lends his money without interest…" (Psalm 15:5). He lends it and doesn't add anything on top for himself. He helps the person and doesn't squeeze them.

explanations.answer: He lends it for a small fee
explanations.explanation: Close, but listen to the exact words. David says he "…lends his money without interest…" (Psalm 15:5). Interest is the thing the psalm says he leaves off. A small fee isn't what this verse talks about.

explanations.answer: He lends it for a short time
explanations.explanation: Good thinking, but the psalm says nothing about how long. It says he "…lends his money without interest…" (Psalm 15:5). The detail is about what he doesn't charge, not about the schedule.
That's it. David says he "…refuses a bribe against the innocent." (Psalm 15:5). The answer is no. He doesn't let money push around somebody who's innocent.
Not this one, friend. The psalm says he "…refuses a bribe against the innocent." (Psalm 15:5). Taking the bribe would mean helping hurt someone innocent. He turns it down.

Ha, I get it, that's how a lot of us start. But the psalm says he "…refuses a bribe against the innocent." (Psalm 15:5). The verse tells us where he lands, and it's a flat no. Whatever the envelope holds, the answer is refuse.
Yes, baker! The psalm ends with "He who does these things will never be shaken." (Psalm 15:5). After that whole list, that's the closing promise. He stays steady.
Good guess, but that's not how the psalm ends. It says "He who does these things will never be shaken." (Psalm 15:5). Hunger doesn't come up anywhere in these five verses.
Nope, friend, and I'd be first in line for that one. The psalm closes with "He who does these things will never be shaken." (Psalm 15:5). It says nothing about age, only that he stays steady.
